To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
anionic sites occur in clusters on the ablumiral aspect of fenestrated capillary endothelium and that they are absent from the fenestral membrane.
the abluminal plasmalemma is extensively decorated with CF, whereas the abluminal membrane of the fenestrae remains free of CF.

the abluminal plasmalemma of endothelial cells is heavily decorated by cationic ferritin (CF), whereas the luminal surface of the endothelial cells is not, and that the fenestral membrane of endothelial cells does not bind CF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, distribution and function of the anionic sites of the endothelial cell.
the distribution of anion sites on the capillary wall.
the identification and characterization of the anionic sites that are responsible for the binding of CF to the basement membrane and to the abluminal face of the endothelial cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the capillary endothelium and basement membrane have an anionic charge which is unevenly distributed, with a preferential concentration on the ablumal aspect of the endothelioplasmic membrane and the lamina rata interna of the basement lamina.

anionic sites on capillary walls are distributed in an ordered planar lattice on the luminal aspect of the basement membrane, on the ablumral aspect of the endothelia, and in the lamina densa, but not in the lamina lucida of the basement membrane.

the capillary endothelium is not a homogeneous, continuous, and impermeable barrier to the passage of macromolecules but rather a heterogeneous and discontinuous barrier with a selective distribution of anionic charges.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endothelial plasalemma is a mosaic structure, composed of a number of different domains with different functions and properties.
the fenestrated endothelium is a permeable membrane that is highly polarized with respect to the charge and the distribution of anionically charged macromolecules.
anionic sites are distributed in a planar lattice on the basement membrane, and that this lattice is replicated on the ablumal aspect of the endothelioplasmic surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the endothelial plasalemma is not homogeneous and that the endothelium can be considered as a sieve with a differentiated permeability.
the abluminal endothelial plasmamembrane is a highly differentiated microdomain, which is not simply a mirror image of the luminal aspect.
anionic sites on endothelial cells are not randomly distributed but rather are organized into a differentiated pattern that is likely involved in the regulation of transendothelial transport.
